The '''1978–79 Bundesliga''' was the 16th season of the [[Bundesliga]], [[West Germany]]'s premier football league. It began on 11 August 1978<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=328555|title=Schedule Round 1|publisher=DFB}}</ref> and ended on 9 June 1979.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=328917|title=Archive 1978/1979 Round 34|publisher=DFB}}</ref> [[1. FC Köln]] were the defending champions.

==Competition modus==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal difference]] and, if still tied, by goals scored. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the three teams with the fewest points were relegated to their respective [[2. Bundesliga]] divisions.

==Team changes to 1978–79==
[[TSV 1860 Munich]], [[1. FC Saarbrücken]] and [[FC St. Pauli]] were relegated to the [[1978–79 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] after finishing in the last three places during 1977–78. They were replaced by [[Arminia Bielefeld]], winners of the 2. Bundesliga Northern Division, [[SV Darmstadt 98]], winners of the Southern Division and [[1. FC Nürnberg]], who won a two-legged promotion play-off against [[Rot-Weiss Essen]].
